newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SPANIARDS MOYA AND COSTA REACH ARIZONA QUARTERS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANIARDS MOYA AND COSTA REACH ARIZONA QUARTERS.

text.p: Spaniards Carlos Moya and Alberto Costa, the third and fourth seeds, were extended Thursday before reaching the quarter-finals of the $328,000 Arizona men's tennis tournament.

Moya, the Australian Open finalist, outlasted stubborn Christian Ruud of Norway 4-6 6-4 7-6 (7-1) to set up a clash with Chris Woodruff, an unseeded American who dismissed another Spaniard Javier Sanchez, 4-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7-4). Sanchez had upset two-time winner Andre Agassi Monday.

Costa, meanwhile, fought off compatriot Sergi Bruguera 6-4 6-7 (5-7) 7-5 to set up a tussle with unseeded Swede Jonas Bjorkman, who knocked off Australian Patrick Rafter of Australia 3-6 6-1 7-6 (7-2).

In the other quarter-final pairings, eighth-seeded American Richey Reneberg will face French qualifier Jerome Golmard while hard-serving Australian Mark Philippoussis will tangle with Byron Black of Zimbabwe.
Rudd served for the match at 5-4 after a break in the seventh game. But Moya broke back and dominated the tiebreaker to gain his third quarterfinal berth of the year.

"He had a chance to beat me but I kept fighting even though I was tired," said Moya, the world's 10th-ranked player who improved his 1997 record to 14-3. "I know until the last ball of the game the match is not over.
"In the tiebreaker, I played very well. I think I'm stronger mentally and they know me. They know they have to fight until the last ball to beat me."
Rudd agreed. "He stepped it up a little bit and was tough in the tiebreaker. He can play well when he wants to and when he does he's one of the best players in the world."
Costa and Bruguera slugged it out from the baseline. Costa held for 6-5 before gaining the decisive service break to edge the two-time French Open winner in the two-hour, 29-minute marathon.
"It was a very tough match, we were fighting a lot," said Costa after gaining the quarters for the second straight year. "I think I was very confident. In the end that's why I was able to win."
Woodruff capitalised on Sanchez's letdown in the third-set tiebreaker. the Spaniard committed a pair of crucial double-faults to take a 5-1 lead before closing out the two-hour, six-minute match.
"I showed a lot heart to hang in there," Woodruff said. The two double-faults really helped."
Bjorkman ran off the last five points in the tiebreaker to eliminate Rafter, a finalist last week in Philadelphia.
"I felt really bad the whole match," Bjorkman said. "I was struggling on my return more than in any match. I was just lucky. I thought I was out of the match."
